text:
samir: Kicking off EU-C7 observability bring-up. Installing Loki (chunk store -> S3), Prometheus (remote_write -> thanos), Tempo, Grafana. Need a short validation checklist + alert templates before we hand this off to SRE tomorrow. Any blockers?

mike: Quick wins: confirm egress for S3 endpoints (we're in a private subnet), and make sure telemetry nodes are labeled so they don't schedule GPU workloads.

priya: Noted. Network team told me NAT gateway is scoped but cost team flagged it — might be cheaper to use VPC endpoint for S3. I'll confirm.

elaine: From infra side, add these to checklist:
- prometheus scrape targets stable (kube-state-metrics, node-exporter)
- loki ingestion pod backpressure checks
- tempo ingestion + query latency under 200ms for sample traces
- grafana datasource tests pass

samir: Good. For Loki, we should run a small ingestion soak test: 50 hosts x 100 lines/sec for 5m and validate tailing queries. Mike, can you drop the promtail helm values you'll use?

mike: Helm values snippet:
```yaml
promtail:
  config:
    positions:
      filename: /data/positions.yaml
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
  nodeSelector:
    telemetry-role: "true"
```
I'll post full chart in the doc repo.

priya: NAT vs VPC endpoint update: network prefers VPC endpoint for S3, avoids NAT charges. Need policy to allow only the observability subnets to use it.

samir: Excellent. Alert templates we need to create before handoff:
- loki_tail_errors_high (>10% ingestion errors per 5m)
- prom_remote_write_retries (sustained > 3 retries)
- tempo_spans_ingest_falloff (drop rate > 2%)
- grafana_proxy_502_rate (>1% of dashboard loads)

elaine: I'll author the Grafana alert rules and the Prometheus recording rules. Quick question: do we want to enable high-cardinality label scrubbing in Loki at ingestion to control costs?

samir: Yes — enable relabel_configs to drop request_ids and other ephemeral tags. Add a note in the runbook about expected ingestion cardinality and cost estimate (approx $X/day at baseline).

deploy-bot: deploy report: loki-0 init -> CrashLoopBackOff (insufficient memory) at 2151234578

mike: Saw that. Increased loki distributor memory requests to 1Gi and restarted. Command I ran: `kubectl set resources deploy loki-distributor -n observability --requests=memory=1Gi`

deploy-bot: loki-0 -> Running at 2151234590

priya: Prometheus remote_write auth failed initially — turned out to be missing service account role to call Thanos receive. Fixed with `rbac: add get/list/watch` to prometheus SA.

elaine: Smoke validation results:
- kubectl get pods -n observability -> all 8/8 Running
- prom scrape: 98% success over 10m (1 scrape target flapped once)
- loki ingestion: 5m soak passed, tail queries OK (<500ms for recent logs)
- tempo: ingest/trace query end-to-end 150ms median
- grafana: dashboards render, templating queries fast

samir: Nice. Remaining items: finalise alert thresholds (elaine), add cost note (samir), and create a handoff checklist with runbook link. I will schedule a 30m handoff tomorrow 09:30 UTC with eng-sre.

mike: I'll add a short emergency rollback plan: scale down promtail + pause remote_write, and set loki to write to local disk only.

samir: Perfect. If nobody objects I'll mark this ready for handoff in the doc and ping eng-sre.

priya: No objections. I'll also confirm VPC endpoint policy by EOD.

elaine: Added alert templates PR: https://git.internal/r/obs-alerts/pull/42 :thumbsup:

samir: Thanks team — handoff scheduled and runbook link is in the doc.
